column15: Fruit-flavored American whiskey (Blackberry, Pineapple variants), confirmed as "Frank's Fiddle American Blackberry Whiskey" via a veli.store listing snippet, but the page itself returned only a maintenance notice when opened this session and no producer/distillery could be identified via a fresh DuckDuckGo/Bing pass (no results beyond that one retailer). Kept low; no positive peat claim (flavored whiskey, not smoke-related).

Corrected kind from blend to brand: Glen Parker is a Speyside single malt (not a malt+grain blend), bottled by Angus Dundee Distillers per a WhiskyRant review, which also notes it may be sourced from more than one distillery ("various distillery left overs"), 40% ABV. Not smoky/peaty per the same review (fermented citrus, cider, apple notes) - none.

Ordinary blended Scotch whisky (malt+grain, min. 3yr oak aging), confirmed via multiple retailers/importers (eulatimport.com, toulouvin.com, whiskydiscounts.com, melcom.com) - budget/generic brand, no producer/distillery identified. Peat downgraded from 'light' to unknown: the only supporting text ('smoky and mineral notes' / 'notas ahumadas y minerales') appears in retailer/importer marketing copy (eulatimport, toulouvin), not the producer's own domain, and there is no Islay/producer-domain corroboration. withheld peat proposal: light per eulatimport.com/toulouvin.com tasting note.

RESOLVED: Glenlassie is NOT a Glenlossie misspelling - it is a genuine, distinct blended Scotch whisky (70% grain / 30% malt) produced by The Tomatin Distillery Co Ltd, named after Robert Burns' 1786 poem 'My Highland Lassie O' (per rareoldwhisky.fr, which states this plainly). Corrected kind from distillery to blend (Whiskybase also lists it as 'Blended Scotch Whisky Glenlassie', 40% ABV, per search results). Tasting notes are cereal/fruity (peach, mirabelle, toasted grain) with no smoke mentioned - none. Do NOT alias this row to glenlossie.

Re-confirmed via the producer's own domain (moldstandart.md): Moldovan whisky made 'by Scottish technology', barley malt, 3-year aged, 40% ABV. No peat/smoke mentioned (aroma described as 'freshness from Scottish mountains') - none.

Heavy-metal band Grave Digger's co-branded whisky/liqueur line, produced by St. Kilian Distillers (Rudenau, Germany; per thewhiskeylover.com retailer). Two researched SKUs: 'Fields of Blood' (47% single malt whisky; official name is plural, the input sample 'Field of Blood' is singular) and 'Berry Metal' (40% berry liqueur on a peated new-make base). The band's own official store (store.grave-digger.de) describes Fields of Blood as made from '100% schottischem Torfrauchmalz' (100% Scottish peated malt) with 'milder Torfrauch' (mild peat smoke) throughout nose/palate/finish - a positive peat claim from the brand's own domain, so set to light rather than withheld. defaultTypeName left empty: range spans single malt whisky and liqueur.

Country corrected from unknown (XX) to Slovakia (SK): Rozetka's own characteristics table states 'Krayina-vyrobnyk: Slovachchyna' (country of manufacture: Slovakia) for both the 3-year and 6-year expressions, and the category listing itself is titled 'Great Barrel vyrobnytstva Slovachchyna'. Description: 'Zmishanyi z lyubov'yu' (blended with care), vanilla/caramel notes, no smoke mentioned - none. No specific producer company identified beyond the Rozetka marketplace seller (CosmoTrade, likely a distributor, not the producer).

Country resolved: Irish whiskey, produced by West Cork Distillers (per maudau.com.ua, echoed by Whiskybase's 'a bottle from West Cork Distillers' and by multiple retailers calling it 'Great Oaks Single Cask Irish Whiskey', incl. Dunnes Stores). 46% ABV. Vanilla/spice profile, no peat/smoke mentioned - none. defaultTypeName left empty (Irish whiskey style/mash bill not confirmed for the full range). Corrected kind from blend to brand.

Corrected kind from blend to distillery: Greenbar Distillery (Los Angeles, CA) is itself the distiller of its organic 'Slow Hand' single malt whiskey (100% malted barley), matured using six wood types (white oak, hickory, maple, mulberry, red oak, grape) rather than smoked - billed as 'LA's first aged whiskey since Prohibition', founded by husband-and-wife Melkon Khosrovian and Litty Mathew. Confirmed via the producer's own domain (the seed round's domain guess had failed on a TLS error; greenbardistillery.com resolved fine this session). No peat/smoke mentioned - none.

Re-confirmed via the producer's own domain this session: Bob Dylan's American whiskey brand (Ascension bourbon, Revival Tennessee bourbon, Refuge rye, Revelation double barrel), distilled at Six Mile Creek Distillery (Ken Pierce, Master Distiller), with a Lead Blender sourcing/blending from multiple distilleries worldwide. No peat/smoke mentioned - none. defaultTypeName left empty (range spans bourbon/rye/tennessee).

Real, well-documented brand - the seed's 'no web presence found' was wrong. Produced by Loch Lomond Group (self-sufficient Scottish distillery group), a malt+grain blend with a history to 1856, aged in American oak, peach/pear/honey/vanilla-toffee profile. The producer's own page explicitly describes 'the gentlest, smoky hint of peat' - a positive peat claim corroborated by the producer's own domain, so set to light rather than withheld. Also sold as a 7-year lightly-peated limited edition. Owner/bottlerSlug set to Loch Lomond Group (live slug loch-lomond).

Confirmed: 'Ichiro's Malt & Grain World Blended Whisky' (malt+grain sourced from around the world, Venture Whisky Ltd, founder Ichiro Akuto; niijima-soken.com, region Saitama) and 'Ichiro's Malt Wine Wood Reserve' (a separate blended-malt line combining Chichibu and Hanyu malt whiskies, wine-cask finished, per multiple retailer/whisky-database listings) both trade under the 'Ichiro's' name. kind=blend fits both sub-lines since neither is a single-distillery single malt. No peat mentioned in either line's tasting notes found this session - kept unknown.

Confirmed via the specific Wikipedia article (not the generic Whisky page used before): historic Kentucky brand relaunched in 2008 by entrepreneur Amir Peay, distilled at the rebuilt James E. Pepper Distillery, 1200 Manchester St, Lexington, KY. Bourbon and rye range, no peat/smoke mentioned - none. defaultTypeName left empty (range spans bourbon and rye).

Real product, not a dead end: 'James Kilton Single Malt Whisky', 44% ABV, sold as 'LGC James Kilton Single Malt' by several Ukrainian retailers whose indexed data names the producer as 'Les Grands Chais' (i.e. Les Grands Chais de France). bauturialcoolice.ro confirms Scotch whisky 'from established Scottish regions' (Speyside/Highlands, not pinned to one) and explicitly unpeated ('nu utilizeaza turba') - none. Corrected kind from blend to brand (single malt, not a malt+grain blend).

column7: Crabbie (John Crabbie & Co., bottled at Bonnington Distillery)
column15: Real single malt, not an anonymous own-label blend: 'Bonnington - James Wyld - Lowland Single Malt Scotch Whisky', 40% ABV, named after the historical Edinburgh whisky trader James Wyld (Port of Leith, est. 1801), whose business later became John Crabbie & Co. Distilled at Bonnington Distillery (Leith; commissioned 2019, production from March 2020), bottled under the Crabbie heritage name. Corrected kind from blend to brand, filled region/legalRegion=lowland and parentSlug=bonnington (live slug). Tasting notes: honey, caramel, malt, oak, floral - no peat/smoke - none.

Country and producer resolved (was fully unknown/unknown): 'Jim Bardett' Blended Scotch Whisky (malt spirits distilled in Scotland, 3yr oak-aged, 40%), produced by Bardinet (French spirits house founded by Paul Bardinet, based in Bordeaux, also known for 'Negrita' rum) - per Rozetka's own characteristics table ('Krayina-vyrobnyk: Velyka Brytaniya', 'Vyd: Blend') and product description naming Bardinet's history directly. No peat/smoke mentioned - none.

Re-confirmed this session via vertumne.com (French importer/distributor Verthemis International): Tibetan Plateau single malt from rare Qingke barley, matured for years in terracotta 'Jiu Hai' amphorae then finished in ex-bourbon/French oak casks. whisky.com and caskers.com (the seed round's sources) were unreachable this session (Cloudflare challenge on both) but the Huzhujinquan attribution is corroborated by consistent independent retailer listing titles seen in search results. No ISO code exists for Tibet/China in the closed country list - XX kept. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere - none. Corrected kind from distillery to brand (Huzhujinquan Distillery is the actual production site; Jiu Hai Bu Gan / Meido are the product/export brand names).

Real product, not a low-priority unknown: 'Joe Got a Gun' Tennessee Whiskey (Single Barrel, Small Batch releases), 40-45% ABV depending on release, aged in charred oak barrels, sourced American whiskey (producing distillery not named on the pages checked). No peat/smoke mentioned (standard charred-oak aging) - none. Corrected kind from blend to brand and filled defaultTypeName=tennessee (multiple independent retailers consistently label the range 'Tennessee Whiskey': onthewhiskey.com, peoplesbourbonreview.com, spiritssquare.com).

Real product: 'John Lee' Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey, 40% ABV, described by one retailer as 'originally produced for the French market' (bottler not named on the pages checked). Vanilla/toffee/corn/honey profile, no peat/smoke - none. Corrected kind from blend to brand and filled defaultTypeName=bourbon (consistent 'Kentucky Straight Bourbon' labeling across independent retailers: bourbonery.com, blue-cask.com, htfw.com).

column7: Crabbie (John Crabbie & Co., bottled at Bonnington Distillery)
column15: Real single malt, sibling release to James Wyld (this batch, slug james-wyld) - not an unresearched budget blend: 'Bonnington - Johnny Cree - Lowland Single Malt Scotch Whisky', 40% ABV, named for Johnny Cree, son of whisky maker James Cree and John Crabbie's daughter Agnes. Distilled at Bonnington Distillery (Leith), bottled under the Crabbie heritage name; aged in bourbon/virgin oak/red wine casks. Corrected kind from blend to brand, filled region/legalRegion=lowland and parentSlug=bonnington (live slug). Honey, caramel, malt, oak, floral notes - no peat/smoke - none. Note for reviewer: Bonnington distillery does also release occasional heavily-peated single-cask expressions under its own name, but the Crabbie-branded James Wyld/Johnny Cree/John Crabbie line is consistently unpeated.

Owner confirmed as Stoli Group (not Sazerac, which the seed round had already correctly ruled out): Kentucky Owl (Bardstown, KY) bourbon+rye brand, per breakingbourbon.com's July 2025 press release ('KENTUCKY OWL, a part of Stoli Group'). No peat/smoke - none. defaultTypeName left empty (bourbon+rye range). FLAG FOR HUMAN REVIEWER: contemporaneous coverage (Jan-Mar 2026) reports Stoli Group filed Chapter 11 in Nov 2024 and converted to Chapter 7 liquidation in early 2026 - Kentucky Owl's ongoing production/ownership may change; worth a fresh check before/soon after this row goes live.

Real, established brand - not a coronation novelty as the seed guessed. 'King Charles' Blended Scotch Whisky (grain+malt), produced by Quality Spirits International (QSI), named for King Charles II's 17th-century legacy (not the current monarch). Confirmed via the producer's own domain: vanilla, smooth/sweet profile, no peat/smoke - none. Award-winning (Scotch Whisky Masters Gold 2023 and 2025, ISC Gold 2024, per IWSC results pages).

Corrected the seed's 'likely discontinued' guess: Kirkcowan is a CURRENT, distinctly-produced single malt spirit at Bladnoch Distillery (Scottish Lowlands) - Bladnoch's own site (Private Casks FAQ) confirms 'Kirkcowan New Make Spirit is different to Bladnoch New Make Spirit ... through differences in the production process', made at the same distillery. Multiple retailers (Whiskybase, Passion for Whisky, svetnapoju.cz, greatwine.co.uk) list bottled 'Bladnoch Kirkcowan' / 'Kirkcowan' single malt releases at 40% ABV, and greatwine.co.uk explicitly calls it an 'Unpeated Lowland Single Malt' - none (this matches Bladnoch's well-established unpeated Lowland house style; not a positive claim needing separate corroboration). Corrected kind from blend to brand and filled parentSlug=bladnoch (live slug).
